workflow.singleFrameButtonTooltip: Sets frame count to 1, active frame 1, and applies the quick start offset for the current film format (same percentages as the FILM FORMAT panel buttons). Fine-tune in the strip preview window, then save as a grid preset if you like.
workflow.singleFrameHintShort: For one full frame with perforation edges: then narrow the grid (Hand tool) and adjust top/bottom margins in the strip window.
workflow.starterSelectTooltip: Pick a film format, or leave empty to use the current selection in the strip panel.
workflow.starterApplyTooltip: Sets 1 frame and the coarse start offset for the chosen (or current) film format (same percentages as FILM FORMAT). Fine-tune in the strip window; save as a grid preset to reuse.
workflow.templatesHint: Tip: when the grid fits, press Save under grid preset — that template is reused on other scans (geometry only).
settings.outputResTooltip: Grid (native) = crop in pixels from the high-resolution strip (scan as loaded, up to the app’s max strip side), not the low-res preview. Other options fit within the frame (letterbox) and may scale up.
settings.arrangeMatrixHint: With all six open: equal tiles on this grid (default sizes). One window: full screen. Two: two columns. Three: three columns. Four or more: this 3×2 grid.
settings.arrangeMatrixModesHint: Pick windows: click a cell to include or exclude the panel number shown there for Auto arrange (blue outline = included). Swap positions: click two cells to swap their numbers (orange outline on the first click).
settings.arrangeAcrossAllDisplaysLabel: Spread windows across all displays: panels 1–6 on successive monitors
settings.arrangeAcrossAllDisplaysHint: When on, the grid above is ignored: open windows are placed in fixed order (1 main, 2 RASTER SETUP, 3 RASTER PREVIEW, 4 OUTPUT, 5 Settings, 6 pixel editor) across screens left to right. If there are more windows than displays, extras are stacked on the last display.
settings.arrangeOnStartupLabel: Auto-arrange windows on startup (after opening preview windows)
settings.windowsGeometryLockedLabel: Lock position and size of all windows (no accidental drag or resize)
settings.windowsGeometryLockedHint: Uncheck to move or resize again. “Arrange windows” and saving settings still apply while locked.
settings.arrowStepTooltip: Movement per arrow key in scan strip preview
settings.arrowStepShiftTooltip: Movement per arrow key with Shift held
settings.preserveGridOnScanNavLabel: Keep grid when Previous/Next/Go to scan (project)
settings.preserveGridOnScanNavTooltip: On: when changing scan strip, current grid adjustment stays (clamped to the new strip). Off: each scan loads its saved lint state (or default grid). “Load scan strip…” always behaves as off.
settings.stripShortcutsHint: Applies to the RASTER SETUP window. Click Change… then press the desired key (with Ctrl, Shift, Alt or Win if needed). Esc cancels. Clear disables the shortcut. After Save settings, active RASTER SETUP windows update immediately.
settings.stripShortcutVerticalAnchorLine: Line #: Up — one step toward top of grid (k−1; Up button, Space, Page Up)
Line #: Down — one step toward bottom (k+1; Down button, Shift+Space, Page Down)
stripPreview.noScanLoaded: No scan strip loaded. Load one from the main window.
stripPreview.anchorRowTitle: Reference line (0…n): 0 = top of grid, n = bottom. For 0<k<n: Hand / Push / T± / B± use split (line fixed). For k=n + link: Push with fixed bottom margin.
stripPreview.verticalAnchorInputTitle: Line index: 0 = top of grid … n = bottom. Up / Page Up / Space = one step toward the top (k−1). Down / Page Down / Shift+Space = one step toward the bottom (k+1). Shortcuts can be changed in Settings.
stripPreview.lineStepUpTitle: One step toward the top of the grid (previous line index, k−1). Same as Space and Page Up.
stripPreview.lineStepDownTitle: One step toward the bottom of the grid (next line index, k+1). Same as Shift+Space and Page Down.
stripWindow.btnRefreshTitle: Reload strip from main window (bitmap + grid). Useful if the view stayed empty.
stripWindow.btnOpenAlignTitle: Open RASTER PREVIEW (strong zoom per frame)
stripWindow.scanGotoRowTitle: Scan strip number (1 = first in project), then Go to

stripWindow.presetBlockTitle: Same list as main window (app data on disk)
stripWindow.zoomStackTitle: Shortcuts: Numpad * = fit width, / = fit height
stripWindow.zoomFitWidthTitle: Fit scan strip width to window (numpad *)
stripWindow.zoomFitHeightTitle: Fit scan strip height to window (numpad /)
stripWindow.panelLinkRowTitle: On: Hand ▲▼, Push and Shift+Push follow reference line (split; at line k=n also fixed bottom on Push). Off: rigid pan.
stripWindow.widthGroupTitle: Grid width: left or right edge only (same step)
stripWindow.heightGroupTitle: Grid height: top or bottom edge only (same step)
stripWindow.pushGroupTitle: Push: at line k=n + link: Y-bottom fixed. For 0<k<n: split (line fixed). Else rigid. Shift+button = to limit.
stripWindow.btnVertUpTitle: Line k=n + link: taller cells (Y-bottom fixed). Else: rigid up. Shift = max.
stripWindow.btnVertDownTitle: Line k=n + link: shorter cells (Y-bottom fixed). Else: rigid down. Shift = max.
stripWindow.stepGroupTitle: Step in preview pixels for move, width and height

stripWindow.scanGotoTitleNoMax: First strip in project = 1 (alphabetical folder order). Save first, then load.
stripWindow.scanGotoTitleWithCur: Strips 1–{max} (current: {cur}). Save project first, then load.
stripWindow.scanGotoTitleRangeOnly: Strips 1–{max}. Save project first, then load.
alignPreview.btnRefreshTitle: Reload strip from main window (same as RASTER SETUP).
alignPreview.zoomFitWidthTitle: Fit scan strip width to the window
alignPreview.zoomFitHeightTitle: Fit visible scan strip height to the window
alignPreview.lockScrollRowTitle: On: after grid changes, view stays at same scroll position. Off: active frame is centered.

overlay.hint: Positioning and sizing of the grid (X/Y, Y-bottom, arrows, width/height, compress/stretch per step (1/10 px), Shift+Compress = max compress, reset, jump TOP/MIDDLE/BOTTOM, zoom, presets with name) happens in the RASTER SETUP window. Quick film format + start offset: FILM FORMAT panel on the left. Below: grid from millimeters or strip pixels, and grid presets (dimensions/offsets only — usable in any project).

overlay.gridPresetSaveTooltip: Save current grid dimensions under this name
overlay.gridPresetLoadTooltip: Apply selected preset to current scan

overlay.mmHeightTooltip: Height of one frame in millimeters
overlay.mmFramesTooltip: Number of frames on the strip

overlay.applyGridTooltip: Adjust grid so cell size matches the given mm as closely as possible

overlay.pxHeightTooltip: One cell height in pixels on the scan strip bitmap
overlay.pxFramesTooltip: Number of frames on the strip
overlay.captureRefPxTooltip: Fill fields from the active frame using the current grid; then fine-tune or apply
overlay.applyGridPxTooltip: Same logic as mm grid: cells in pixels, centered horizontally, spare height at bottom when possible

frameGenerator.pauseTooltip: 0 = no pause; useful for corrections or test run

pixelEditor.hint: Paint over dust or unwanted pixels on the active frame with the left mouse button. Eyedropper picks a color. Brush mode “Underlying scan” clones grain from the scan next to the brush (pick left/right/above/below toward clean area) for natural blends. Right-click or Ctrl+Z undoes strokes. Feather softens the brush edge. Edits apply to previews and frame export while the strip is loaded. To write painted frames to disk, choose a pixel editor folder and use Previous / Next (each step saves the current frame as PNG if it has paint). Raster setup still saves grid settings only, not pixel layers in the project file. The optional source folder (scans) is only for the pixel editor; Raster setup keeps the project strip. Use ◀ File / File ▶ to step through images in that folder.
pixelEditor.brushModeTooltip: Solid color, or clone texture from the underlying scan for smoother, natural blends
pixelEditor.sampleDirTooltip: Direction from brush center toward clean film: pixels are taken from there (one brush radius away)
pixelEditor.zoomModeTooltip: How the frame is scaled inside the preview area

videoExport.hint: Export from project scans or from a folder with frames. Multiple formats: ProRes (best quality), FFV1 (lossless), HEVC, H.264. Frames folder defaults to Frame generator Target folder. Under “Uniform frame size for video”, choose letterbox or fill without bars (see tooltip).

videoExport.outputResolutionTooltip: Same choices as Frame generator and Settings (SD through UHD). For Custom, set width and height under Settings.
videoExport.uniformFitTooltip: When crop sizes differ: “Letterbox” pads with black to the largest frame (nothing cropped). “Fill” scales so the image covers the full frame and trims excess edges (no black bars). Also applies when a fixed output resolution is chosen.
videoExport.uniformFitCover: Fill (no bars, edges may be cropped)
